correctness.rationale: In a cubic triangle-free graph of this order, the first force from three black vertices leaves a closed neighborhood whose leaves each have two white neighbors, so at least four seeds are required. For four seeds, a one-row set needs a consecutive triple for a first force and cannot advance unless the fourth extends it. With three seeds on one row and v_0 on the other, omission of u_0 makes the only possible first force stall; with u_0 present, exactly one horizontal neighbor of u_0 must be initially selected. After reflection, choose the force u_0→u_{−1}; the third upper seed must then be at ±2 to enable another force. Other initially legal choices do not invalidate this necessity: a stalled closure after any legal sequence contains every reachable forced vertex, by monotonicity. With two seeds on each row, a first force requires an adjacent row pair with a shared column and stalls if the opposite pair is nonadjacent. With adjacent pairs the relative shifts are exactly −1,0,1. Each surviving template makes two adjacent full rungs, which propagate both ways. The types are disjoint and have the claimed multiplicities. Independently verified all five rows of the exact intersection-three table by triple incidence, using integer anchors −5,…,5 and separately cyclic n=6,…,15; replay: python3 /workspace/review_ladder_overlap.py. Any candidate sharing a vertex has an anchor in that integer interval up to reduction, and all its columns and the representative's lie in [−7,8], where reduction is injective for n≥16. This certifies the table on the entire stated range, not by extrapolation. The degree polynomial and 48n follow by summing degrees. Aligned states for consecutive anchors are joined through a shifted state, and the table attaches all other types. The supplied scripts and saved outputs were inspected, not executed; the n=5 profile is only supporting boundary evidence.
